topics.title: Family
topics.subtitle: Words for relatives
topics.note: Your family speaks a Montenegrin-Dalmatian blend — words like dida and kukumar are your family's words, not mistakes. In Montenegrin, grandpa may also be deda.

lines.supportText: Good afternoon! What is your name?
My name is Lena. And you?

lines.targetText: Zovem se Sam. Drago mi je!
lines.supportText: My name is Sam. Nice to meet you!
Nice to meet you too! Goodbye.

topics.title: At a Café
topics.subtitle: Order like a local
topics.note:
Hoću = I want, Neću = I don't want.
Words ending in -a often change to -u after these: kafa → Hoću kafu, voda → Hoću vodu.

lines.supportText: Good afternoon! What can I get you?
Here they are, on the towel.

items.supportText: What do you like to do?

lines.targetText: Dobro došli u Crnu Goru! Pasoš, molim.
Hvala! Jedva čekam da vidim porodicu.
lines.supportText: Thank you! I can't wait to see my family.

items.supportText: How long have you been here?

items.targetText: Ovo mi je prvi put ovdje.
items.supportText: This is my first time here.

lines.supportText: Good evening! Here is the menu.
Okay, I'll have the fish, please.

topics.title: Family Gathering
topics.subtitle: A full conversation at the table

items.supportText: It was wonderful to see you.

lines.targetText: Živjeli! Hvala na ručku, bilo je divno.
lines.supportText: Cheers! Thank you for lunch, it was wonderful.

items.supportText: Cyrillic: А а — "ah", as in auto (car)
Cyrillic: Б б — "b", as in brat (brother)
Cyrillic: Ц ц — "ts", as in cvijet (flower)
Cyrillic: Ч ч — hard "ch", as in čokolada
Cyrillic: Ћ ћ — soft "ch", as in ćevapi
Cyrillic: Д д — "d", as in dijete
Cyrillic: Ђ ђ — soft "j", as in đak
Cyrillic: Џ џ — hard "j", as in džak
Cyrillic: Љ љ — "ly", as in ljubav
Cyrillic: Њ њ — "ny", as in njiva
Cyrillic: Ш ш — "sh", as in šuma
Cyrillic: Ж ж — "zh", as in žena
